item.title: US Automakers Need More Than Peace With Canada
item.description: The US and Canada appear poised to clinch a deal on an industry central to the North American free-trade battle: autos. As ever with President Donald Trump’s trade war, a fog of uncertainty and potential U-turns persists. In this case, the details that have emerged suggest the deal would represent a good first step for Detroit, but only that. Don’t tell the president, but foreign automakers look like more immediate beneficiaries.
item.dc:creator: Liam Denning

item.title: Federal Reserve Undermined by Treasury’s Aggressive Buyback Strategy
item.description: That was quicker than anyone surely imagined. It’s been just three months since Kevin Warsh took the helm of the Federal Reserve and he’s already being undermined by a White House that gave him the job.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Levin

item.title: Lessons from Princess Diana’s Battles With the British Press
item.description: On the evening of Aug. 30, 1997, a Saturday, I was the duty editor at Time magazine in New York, in charge of updating stories as we headed to press. It had been newslessly quiet. Most of the city — indeed, the US — was already enjoying the three-day Labor Day holiday. In Paris, however, it was already Sunday Aug. 31, and at around 12:30 am the French capital had become the epicenter of a news event that swiftly swept the world. item.title: German Pension Reform Is a Necessary Shift Toward More Risk
item.description: My first job after getting my doctorate in economics was helping to set up a defined-contribution pension plan for a corporation in Hamburg. I spent many hours hammering out the details with a pair of German actuaries, Horst and Wolfgang.
item.dc:creator: Allison Schrager

item.title: Nolan's ‘Odyssey’ Has a Worthy French Competitor
item.description: The political movie of the year tells the story of an odyssey: A grizzled war veteran in exile, desperate to return home to his family and country, leading a rump of an army through impossible odds as massacres, vengeance and mutiny rage.
item.dc:creator: Lionel Laurent

item.title: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent Is At Odds With Fed Chair Kevin Warsh
item.description: The Treasury secretary’s “big toolkit” might do more to break the economy than fix it.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Karl

item.title: India’s UPI Needs Reform, Not US Pressure
item.description: US entanglement in India’s regulatory weeds is becoming a prickly political issue for New Delhi.
item.dc:creator: Andy Mukherjee

item.title: Unitree's Humanoids Have a Long March to Usefulness
item.description: Fresh off a blockbuster public markets debut, Unitree Robotics’ founder Wang Xingxing conceded that his company still hasn’t figured out how to make humanoids truly useful.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Thorbecke

item.title: Mexico's Urban Chaos Can Be Tamed by a High-Rise Revolution
item.description: It’s a familiar sight across Mexico’s urban landscape: cities every time more congested, with inadequate public transportation and tortuous journeys from one end to the other. Traffic is a problem across Latin America and beyond, but Mexico City has more than earned its rank by some measures as the world’s most congested city.
item.dc:creator: Juan Pablo Spinetto

item.title: Fake Political Poll in LA Mayoral Race Bodes Poorly for Democracy
item.description: In late July, as Americans were preparing for another round of high-stakes midterm primaries, top elections officials were on a webinar, warning about the dangers of prediction markets — specifically how both Kalshi and Polymarket are ripe for manipulation by bad actors looking to influence public opinion to turn a profit.
item.dc:creator: Erika D. Smith

item.title: Kansas Senate Race: Adam Hamilton Could Break Democrats' Losing Streak
item.description: Democrats have found the seemingly perfect cardboard cutout to try to win a US Senate seat in ruby-red Kansas for the first time in almost 100 years: a mainstream megachurch pastor. With the political atmosphere turning more toxic by the day for Republicans, Adam Hamilton is an intriguing candidate who could pose a real threat in November.
item.dc:creator: David M. Drucker

item.title: Data Centers Going Off-Grid Doesn’t Make Them Good Neighbors
item.description: As a forest of pitchforks approaches America’s data centers, Big Tech can turn to a time-tested strategy: Hiding. As in, behind the meter. That phrase refers to onsite power generation that can offer backup for data centers or, at the extreme, let them bypass the electricity grid completely.
item.dc:creator: Liam Denning
